scope: Independent full source-level semantic review of all authored mathematical definitions and proofs, plus Audit.lean; no authored mathematical files were changed. Separate root validation supplies the fresh build and strict replay evidence.
bilingual_source: Both the supplied English and Chinese versions contain the same positive exponent (d-1)/2 and the same symmetric-difference relative-volume approximation criterion.
The English word facets fixes codimension-one faces; the Chinese face-count wording is naturally read in the same sense in this bilingual statement.

The source mentions an exact constant in the optimal approximation order. The standard leading/optimal-order constant is finite, positive, and independent of epsilon; all three formal readings make this interpretation explicit.
A dimension-uniform assertion includes d=2. Refuting the rate for that dimension suffices, whether all positive errors or only sufficiently small positive errors were intended.

definition_review.ambient_space: Space d is EuclideanSpace R (Fin d), Mathlib PiLp 2. Its norm is the square root of the sum of coordinate squares; the closed ball is genuinely the Euclidean unit ball, not the product/sup-norm ball.
definition_review.polytope: IsPolytope is the convex hull of an arbitrary finite subset of the ambient Euclidean space. No containment, symmetry, inscribed/circumscribed, or regularity restrictions replace the source class. Degenerate/empty hulls are allowed, but the contradiction is universal over all natural counts and does not exploit such cases.
definition_review.facets: IsFacet requires a nonempty proper exposed face and intrinsic affine dimension one below that of P. Mathlib IsExposed expresses maximization of a continuous linear functional over P; nonemptiness prevents its empty-set clause being used as a facet, and properness excludes the whole P. Finrank is taken in a finite-dimensional real ambient space, so it does not silently represent infinite rank.
definition_review.volume: Approximates uses actual set symmetric difference and canonical Euclidean volume, with ENNReal.ofReal epsilon. For positive errors the factor is exactly the nonnegative real epsilon. Finite convex hulls and closed balls are compact/measurable; the definition does not replace Lebesgue error by a combinatorial surrogate.
definition_review.finite_counts: HasFacetCount P n is a nonempty equivalence Fin n to the subtype of all geometric facets. No Nat.card default, sInf default, or free cardinality value is used. exists_facet_count follows from a proved finiteness statement and facet_count_unique follows from finite equivalence.
definition_review.finiteness_bridge: finite_exposed_faces expresses each exposed face as closure(convexHull(extremePoints F)). Its extreme points are among those of P and hence among the finite generators. The finite powerset image therefore covers every exposed face. The compactness, convexity, exposed-to-extreme, and Krein-Milman uses match their Mathlib meanings.
definition_review.minimum: IsMinimumFacetCount contains an actual admissible polytope with the stated count and a lower bound against every admissible natural count. minimum_exists_iff proves equivalence with existence of any approximant, using well ordering only after obtaining a finite counted approximant. minimum_unique proves uniqueness. It is an attained minimum relation, not a totalized numerical function.

quantifier_review.exact: PrintedExactFormula chooses c>0 and delta>0 first, then requires for every 0<epsilon<delta an actual minimizing count equal to c*epsilon^((d-1)/2). Constants cannot depend on epsilon.
quantifier_review.theta: PrintedThetaOrder chooses a,b,delta>0 and then requires every sufficiently small positive error to have an attained minimum witness within the positive two-sided bounds. Choosing n separately at each epsilon does not weaken the integer contradiction.
quantifier_review.asymptotic: PrintedAsymptoticConstant chooses c>0 before every positive tolerance eta, then an interval and actual minimum witnesses satisfying the ratio-to-one estimate. Since minimum counts are unique wherever they exist, this relational version faithfully expresses the usual asymptotic assertion. No epsilon=0 division is used.
quantifier_review.bridge: Exact implies theta with a=b=c. Asymptotic implies theta by eta=1/2, positivity of c*epsilon^p, and bounds c/2 and 2c. The weaker upper constant 2c is valid.
quantifier_review.filter_auxiliary: The separate Vanishing module also treats Mathlib Asymptotics.IsEquivalent along nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0). Its multiplication-factor characterization and extraction of a positive interval correctly yield a two-sided square-root sandwich.

independent_mathematical_reasoning: For any a,b,delta>0 let t=min(sqrt(delta),1/b)/2 and epsilon=t^2. Then 0<epsilon<delta, sqrt(epsilon)=t, and b*t<1.
Any natural number n satisfying a*sqrt(epsilon)<=n<=b*sqrt(epsilon) would obey 0<n<1. This is impossible, including n=0 because the lower bound is strictly positive.

dimension_two_power identifies the source real exponent exactly with sqrt(epsilon). The final dimension-two theorem applies the universal integer gap to the n supplied by the actual geometric-rate predicate.

Consequently the formalized exact formula, positive leading asymptotic, and positive optimal two-sided order are false in dimension two, establishing the negation of the dimension-uniform claim as printed.

The geometry assumptions need not be consumed in the last contradiction: an impossibility for every natural count is a stronger necessary-condition obstruction. This is not a vacuous implication from an artificially impossible geometric premise.

No independent construction of approximants at every positive error is logically required to refute the claimed existence-and-rate statement. The source assertion itself promises these minimum witnesses; the proof rules out their asserted numerical behavior.
limits: The result concerns the exponent printed in both sources; it does not settle the sign-corrected negative-exponent problem or supply its optimal constant.
Positive leading/optimal-order constants are used. A degenerate unrestricted c=0 exact formula and a bare one-sided big-O formulation are not claimed to be refuted by this arithmetic argument.
The source does not spell out positivity, but calling c_d the constant in the optimal approximation order makes this standard positivity interpretation appropriate; the report states it explicitly.
This is semantic approval of the identified candidate, not maintainer acceptance, eligibility verification, or permission to publish. Packaging and portable-verifier review are separate.
